evals.prompt: I want a skill that sets up my local dev environment: creates a symlink, appends a line to .git/info/exclude, merges some entries into .vscode/settings.json, and then verifies all of it. Write it.
evals.expected_output: Routes the deterministic mutation and verification into a bundled script with an exit-code contract, keeps user interaction and reporting in prose, and produces SKILL.md plus the script and evals.
expectations: Identifies the symlink, exclude-file, settings merge, and verification steps as low-freedom work belonging in a bundled script.
Keeps user-facing decisions and the final report in SKILL.md prose rather than in the script.
Gives the script a non-interactive argparse interface with distinct exit codes per failure gate.
Specifies structured output the agent can branch on rather than prose the agent must parse.
Requires the script to be idempotent so a second run is a no-op.
Creates evals/evals.json alongside the skill.

evals.prompt: Write me a skill for reviewing pull requests in our house style. It should weigh readability, test coverage, and whether the change matches the ticket.
evals.expected_output: Stays in prose because the task is judgment-driven, and does not invent a script for it.
expectations: Classifies PR review as high-freedom work where multiple approaches are valid and context decides.
Does not bundle a script to perform the review judgment.
Expresses the guidance as goals and constraints rather than a rigid step sequence.
Does not claim the skill needs a script in order to be acceptable.

evals.prompt:
My skill never seems to activate. It is installed at ~/.copilot/skills/db-helper/ and `copilot skill list` shows it as enabled. Here it is. The instructions inside are really detailed and correct.

---
name: db-helper
description: Helps with the database.
---

# DB Helper

(200 lines of correct, detailed instructions)
evals.expected_output: Confirms the skill is discoverable and enabled, then diagnoses the description as the cause and rewrites it with concrete triggering vocabulary, without reworking the body.
expectations: Confirms the skill is installed in a discovered location and enabled before blaming the description.
States that retrieval matches against the description only, so the body's quality is irrelevant to activation.
Rewrites the description to lead with what the skill does plus an explicit 'Use this skill when' clause.
Adds concrete vocabulary a user would actually type, such as tool names, commands, or error strings.
Does not attribute the failure to the length or wording of the skill body.

evals.prompt: Review this skill of mine. Step 3 says to exclude the `installer` and `experimental` packages, and step 6 configures the parent directory that contains all the packages including those two.
evals.expected_output: Reports the contradiction between two statements of one rule as a defect and proposes the single-statement fix.
expectations: Identifies that one rule is stated in two places and that the copies now disagree.
Reports it as a defect with severity rather than as a wording preference.
Proposes expressing the exclusion rule exactly once so both steps become consistent.
Does not resolve the contradiction by adding a third statement or a clarifying note.

evals.prompt: Add a validation step to my skill: it should confirm with `copilot skill list --json` that every directory I registered with `copilot skill add` actually got registered.
evals.expected_output: Runs the command to establish its real output shape before writing the assertion, and discovers that it reports skills rather than registered directories.
expectations: Runs `copilot skill list --json` and inspects real output before writing the validation step.
Determines that entries describe individual skills whose path is a leaf skill directory, not the registered directory.
Writes the check against the verified shape, for example prefix matching or reading skillDirectories from settings.
Does not write a plausible-sounding assertion based on the command's name alone.

evals.prompt: My SKILL.md is 900 lines. Should I break it up?
evals.expected_output: Applies progressive disclosure by criterion, splitting volatile, long, or mutually exclusive content into references and keeping the decision spine in SKILL.md.
expectations: Recommends splitting because the body is loaded whole on trigger and competes with conversation context.
Splits on volatility, length, or mutual exclusivity rather than by topic for tidiness.
Keeps the routing or decision logic in SKILL.md and moves detail into references/.
Notes the roughly 5000-token guidance for the body as a recommendation, not a hard limit.

evals.prompt: I want my skill to always have the current git diff available, so I'll put a line with !`git diff HEAD` in the SKILL.md. I use both Copilot CLI and Claude Code.
evals.expected_output: Flags the syntax as a Claude Code extension that will not work in Copilot CLI, and offers the portable alternative.
expectations: States that dynamic command injection with the ! syntax is a Claude Code extension and is not in the open spec.
States that it does not work in Copilot CLI, where the line would be treated as literal text.
Offers the portable alternative of instructing the agent to run the command as a normal step.
Does not present the syntax as generally available.

evals.prompt: Here's the script for my new skill. It does the whole setup in one shot and prints a summary at the end so the user knows what happened.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the scripting decision but requires an exit-code contract, structured output, idempotency, and tests, and moves the user-facing summary back to the agent.
expectations: Requires distinct exit codes per failure gate instead of a single pass/fail.
Requires structured output on stdout that the agent can branch on.
Requires the script to be idempotent on a second run.
Requires unit tests, on the grounds that verifiability is the main justification for scripting.
Moves the human-readable summary out of the script and into the agent's reporting step.

evals.prompt: Write a skill that wires up a project, and use json5 to parse the JSONC settings file so we keep the comments.
evals.expected_output: Checks whether the dependency is actually available and handles its absence rather than assuming it.
expectations: Verifies whether the parser is available rather than assuming it is installed.
Notes that a dependency absent on a clean machine turns the whole skill into a failure.
Prefers a standard-library approach, or declares the requirement explicitly in frontmatter or documentation.
Provides a defined behavior for the comment-preserving case rather than silently destroying comments.

evals.prompt: Review the local-hve-core skill in this repo at skills/local-hve-core/.
evals.expected_output: Applies the review order against the real files, leading with availability and trigger quality, and reports defects with severity instead of rewriting.
expectations: Reads the actual SKILL.md and evals in the named directory rather than reviewing from assumption.
Checks the description against how a user would actually phrase the request, first.
Checks whether any step makes the model re-derive a deterministic procedure.
Checks for rules stated in more than one place and whether the copies agree.
Verifies claims about command behavior against the real commands rather than accepting them.
Checks whether evals cover failure branches and not only the happy path.
Reports findings as defects with severity rather than returning a wholesale rewrite.
Runs scripts/validate_skill.py against the skill and clears or reports its findings.

evals.prompt: I fixed a bug in skills/local-hve-core/: it asserted that `copilot skill list --json` reports registered directories, but it reports individual skills. Anything else I should do before I commit?
evals.expected_output: Requires adding the eval that would have caught the bug, in the same change.
expectations: Requires adding an eval expectation covering the fixed bug in the same change.
Requires the expectation to be objectively checkable rather than subjective.
Checks whether the same wrong assumption about the command appears elsewhere in the skill.
Runs scripts/validate_skill.py before the commit.

evals.prompt:
Here is my new skill. Is it ready to commit?

---
name: Repo_Setup
description: Sets things up.
---

# Repo Setup

See [the guide](references/guide.md) for details.
evals.expected_output: Runs the structural validator, reports the mechanical defects it finds, and does not hand-check them by eye.
expectations: Runs scripts/validate_skill.py rather than inspecting the structure manually.
Reports that the name is not kebab-case and does not match the directory.
Reports the broken relative link to references/guide.md.
Reports that evals/evals.json is missing.
Also flags the vague description as a separate, non-mechanical defect.

evals.prompt: I have two skills: one for authoring skills and one for writing prompts. Users keep getting the wrong one. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Treats overlapping descriptions as the defect and adds negative boundaries to both.
expectations: Identifies the overlap as a description problem rather than a body problem.
Adds an explicit 'Do not use for' clause naming the sibling skill to at least one description.
Differentiates the triggering vocabulary so each description claims distinct situations.
Recommends an eval where a near-miss phrasing must not load the skill.

evals.prompt: Classify these two skills for Copilot CLI and Claude Code. `api-conventions` is background guidance the agent should apply automatically, but it should not appear as a slash command. `deploy-production` must run only when I explicitly invoke it. Both skills should remain portable to other Agent Skills hosts.
evals.expected_output: Treats model and user invocation as independent controls, configures the background skill as agent-only and deployment as user-only, and explains that unsupported hosts may ignore both fields.
expectations: Sets `user-invocable: false` on `api-conventions` and does not disable model invocation for it.
Sets `disable-model-invocation: true` on `deploy-production` and leaves user invocation enabled.
Explains that the two fields control independent invocation paths rather than naming mutually exclusive skill types.
States that Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, and Claude Code support the fields.
States that neither field is part of the open Agent Skills specification and another host may ignore them.
Does not present invocation metadata as a replacement for tool permissions or user approval gates.
